skill.name: exploratory-data-analysis
skill.description: Analyze scientific data files across chemistry, genomics, microscopy, spectroscopy, omics, and general formats with format-aware markdown reports.
skill.summary: Analyze scientific data files and create format-aware EDA reports.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, code fences, scientific terms, or reference documentation for local file handling. One confirmed issue remains: scripts/eda_analyzer.py writes reports to a caller-controlled output path, which can overwrite files if misused. Generated reports also include absolute input paths, creating a low-severity privacy risk.

remediation.suggestion: Constrain output paths to the workspace or require confirmation before overwriting an existing file.

remediation.issue: Absolute input path appears in reports
remediation.suggestion: Record only the filename or a relative path unless the user requests full paths.

remediation.issue: Archive handling is documented without safety guidance
remediation.suggestion: Document size limits, trusted paths, and extraction controls for ZIP or TAR based workflows.

content.value_statement: Scientific files often hide structure, quality issues, and metadata across many formats. This skill detects formats and produces practical EDA reports for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Detects scientific file types by extension across major research domains.
Loads format notes from local reference files for supported extensions.
Summarizes CSV, TSV, JSON, NumPy, HDF5, FASTA, FASTQ, and common image files.
Computes dimensions, metadata, missing values, summary statistics, sequence metrics, and image intensity metrics.
Generates markdown reports with format details, findings, and next analysis recommendations.
limitations: Many vendor formats require optional Python libraries that may not be installed.
Large files may need sampling to avoid long runtimes or high memory use.
The analyzer supports exploration, not full domain-specific analysis workflows.
Generated reports may include local file paths unless the script is adjusted.

use_cases.title: Review a new dataset
use_cases.description: Profile unfamiliar instrument or assay files before choosing a processing method.

use_cases.title: Assess sequence files
use_cases.description: Inspect FASTA or FASTQ files for sequence counts, length ranges, and quality signals.

use_cases.title: Document data archives
use_cases.description: Generate consistent markdown summaries for datasets before storage, review, or handoff.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize one file
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [file path] with the exploratory-data-analysis skill. Identify the format, structure, quality notes, and recommended next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Create a report
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the analyzer script on [file path] and save the report as [report path]. Explain any missing libraries or read errors.

prompt_templates.title: Compare related files
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these files: [paths]. Compare formats, dimensions, quality issues, and shared preprocessing needs.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: For [file path] and research goal [goal], inspect the format notes, summarize risks, and propose a validated analysis workflow.

output_examples.input: Explore a FASTQ file from a sequencing run.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies FASTQ, samples reads, reports read counts, length ranges, mean quality, and recommends filtering and alignment checks.

output_examples.input: Review a CSV file of experiment results.
output_examples.output: The skill reports row and column counts, data types, missing values, numeric summaries, and suggestions for outlier review and correlations.
The skill reports image dimensions, mode, value range, mean intensity, page count when available, and image analysis recommendations.

best_practices: Run analysis on a sample first when files are very large.
Install only the format libraries needed for the file under review.
Review generated reports before sharing them outside the project.
anti_patterns: Do not assume unsupported vendor formats are fully parsed.
Do not share reports that contain private file paths or sensitive sample names.
Do not run the script on untrusted archives without separate extraction controls.

faq.question: Which file types does it support?
faq.answer: It covers chemistry, genomics, microscopy, spectroscopy, omics, and common scientific data formats through reference files.

faq.question: Does it run automatically on every file?
faq.answer: No. Use it when a user asks to inspect or summarize a scientific data file.

faq.question: Can it analyze very large files?
faq.answer: Yes, but large files should be sampled or processed with memory-aware tools.

faq.question: What reports does it create?
faq.answer: It creates markdown reports with file metadata, format notes, summary metrics, findings, and recommended next steps.

faq.question: Does it require extra libraries?
faq.answer: Some formats require optional libraries such as pandas, h5py, Biopython, Pillow, or domain-specific readers.

faq.question: Is it safe to share generated reports?
faq.answer: Review reports first because they may include file paths, sample identifiers, or dataset-derived metadata.
